title: Outgoing webhook delivery with retries
description: Send webhooks from a multi-tenant server app: tenant-scoped endpoint management behind an authorize hook, Standard Webhooks signatures with secret rotation, a durable delivery queue written on the caller's transaction, a leased worker with per-attempt timeouts, exponential backoff with jitter, dead-lettering and manual replay, an SSRF guard checked at registration and send time, a PostgreSQL store and a Fetch management adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build, Web Crypto (crypto.subtle HMAC, getRandomValues, randomUUID), AbortSignal.timeout, btoa/atob, structuredClone and the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno and Next.js route handlers. The resolver must be injected (for example node:dns lookup), so edge runtimes without DNS need their own resolver.
Framework-neutral core; run runOnce from your own scheduler or worker loop and mount the management adapter on one catch-all route.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlWebhookStore with your query executor; elsewhere implement WebhookDeliveryStore with a unique (endpoint_id, event_id), an atomic leased claim, lease renewal and completion fenced by the lease owner.

Pass fetch (globalThis.fetch, or a pinning fetch that connects only to context.addresses), resolveHost (for example node:dns/promises lookup with {all: true}) and authorize(actor, tenantId, action) backed by your membership and role checks.
Call enqueue({tenantId, eventId, type, data}, {tx}) with an executor bound to the transaction that makes the business change; use a stable eventId per business event.

Run runOnce({workerId}) on a schedule with a unique workerId per process; keep leaseMs at least max(timeoutMs x ceil(limit / concurrency), timeoutMs + 1 s); each attempt renews the lease when it starts.
Optionally pass a secretBox to encrypt stored secrets with your key management service.
Mount createWebhookEndpointsHandler under one prefix with authenticate(request) from your session layer and exact allowedOrigins.
limitations: Delivery is at least once: a worker that crashes after the receiver accepted a request sends it again after the lease expires, with the same webhook-id, so receivers must deduplicate.

The SSRF guard checks the addresses the injected resolver returns; the default global fetch resolves the hostname again, so a DNS rebinding between check and connect is closed only by a fetch that connects to context.addresses (for example an undici Agent with a pinned lookup). Proxies configured in the runtime bypass the address check.
Secrets are stored in plaintext unless a secretBox is supplied; anyone with table read access can sign webhooks.
The endpoint-per-tenant limit is checked before insert and is not atomic under concurrent creates.
Event types match exactly (no wildcards); asymmetric v1a signatures, Retry-After, automatic endpoint disabling after repeated failures and row pruning are not implemented.

The in-memory store ignores the tx argument and is for tests and prototypes only; the SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which runs one connection, so FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED across separate connections is not exercised there.
Production database correctness, secret custody, receiver behavior and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: Standard Webhooks signing: webhook-id/timestamp/signature, v1 HMAC of id.timestamp.body, whsec_ secrets
backoff doubles with jitter; redirects not followed; private, loopback and metadata addresses refused
options: maxAttempts (10); backoff.baseMs, backoff.maxMs (30 s, 6 h); timeoutMs per attempt (10 s)
maxPayloadBytes (256 KiB); rotationGraceMs (24 h); allowHttp (default false, tests only)

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/webhook-delivery.test.mjs tests/webhook-delivery-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: signatures use Standard Webhooks headers and verify with the webhook-verification module's verifyStandardWebhook
after rotation every active secret signs until the previous secret's grace period ends; endpoint views never contain secret values; a secretBox seals stored secrets
network errors, timeouts and non-2xx responses retry with exponential backoff and jitter from an injected random, then become dead after maxAttempts
manual replay requeues a dead or succeeded delivery with the same webhook-id and a fresh attempt budget
enqueue writes one delivery per (event, endpoint), idempotent on the event id and filtered by event type and tenant
each attempt has its own AbortSignal timeout (the default AbortSignal.timeout aborts with TimeoutError) and a fetch that ignores the signal still releases the worker
response bodies are read up to maxResponseBytes and the stream is cancelled

the SSRF guard refuses http, URL credentials, localhost and metadata names, decimal, octal, hex and shortened IPv4 forms and private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, multicast, ULA, IPv4-mapped and documentation addresses at registration and at send time
fetch uses redirect manual and a 3xx response is a failed attempt
endpoint CRUD, secret rotation, delivery reads and replay require authorize(actor, tenantId, action) to return true; other tenants get not-found and never receive deliveries
a crashed worker's lease is reclaimed after expiry, the stale worker's complete is refused while the new owner's attempt is in flight, and crash loops stop at maxAttempts
each attempt renews the lease when it starts, so a slow lane never lets another worker resend its last item; an item reclaimed before its turn is skipped
runOnce honours limit and concurrency and refuses a lease shorter than the batch can take
HTTP adapter: secret shown only on create and rotate, 401 without a user, 403 for unauthorized actors and bad origins, 404 across tenants, 400 for refused URLs, 409 for non-replayable deliveries
on PostgreSQL, delivery rows roll back with the caller's transaction and commit with it, and survive a restart
four concurrent workers over 40 deliveries send each exactly once on PGlite; concurrent rotations never lose a secret

changes: First release: core delivery engine, Standard Webhooks signing, SSRF guard, in-memory store, PostgreSQL schema and store, and Fetch endpoint-management adapter.
